title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Scene hazards, vital signs and rapid-response decisions test whether you can think clearly when every clue matters.

landing.intro: Scene hazards, vital signs, emergency maths and calm judgement. Can you think clearly when every clue matters?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten entrance-style questions across anatomy, observations, numeracy, communication, safety and priority judgement. It tests careful reasoning rather than local protocols or operational procedures.

Choose the best answer using only the information shown. Safe options favour recognising risk, communicating clearly and seeking appropriate qualified support.

This is not an accredited paramedic entrance exam, clinical assessment, qualification, training course or source of emergency advice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer each time. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, skill breakdown and complete answer review after the final question.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited paramedic entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Emergency procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local guidance and appropriately qualified emergency professionals.

checkpoint.finalAdNote: One short ad, then your results.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your paramedic entrance score and six-area breakdown are ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Emergency Standout
profile-1.copy: You combined excellent foundational knowledge with calm, evidence-led judgement across the entire response assessment. Scene hazards, changing observations and communication details stayed clear even when the final cases became demanding.

profile-2.title: The Rapid-Response Natural
profile-2.copy: You showed a strong feel for the knowledge and judgement behind safe emergency response. Most of the assessment's trend, numeracy, safety and handover traps did not pull you off course.

profile-3.title: The Calm Scene Solver
profile-3.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, scene decisions and multi-clue cases with steady reasoning. A few finer handover and observation details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profile-4.title: The Steady Responder
profile-4.copy: You built a solid result by following visible evidence and treating safety seriously. Your strongest area shows where your emergency-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profile-5.title: The Promising Candidate
profile-5.copy: You solved a good share of the assessment and showed useful instincts across several response areas. The answer review will reveal which foundations are ready for another look.

profile-6.title: The First-Response Explorer
profile-6.copy: The assessment uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful, safety-first judgement. Every reviewed answer is a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind calm emergency thinking.

score.passed: You passed the paramedic entrance challenge!

paramedic-r1q1.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
answers: Heart
Lungs
Brain
Bones

paramedic-r1q5.question: Which opening makes the clearest handover?
answers: Something changed earlier, probably
Here are all the minor details in random order
At 14:20, breathing became faster and alertness decreased
I already know exactly what caused it

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse 80 then 92 then 108, with pallor and dizziness

paramedic-r5q4.question: What is the best interpretation of this pattern?
answers: The record is unchanged
The combined trend suggests deterioration needing prompt qualified assessment
Only the first number matters
The symptoms can be ignored because no diagnosis is shown

paramedic-r2q4.question: Which statement best describes the kidneys?
answers: They exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
They remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance
They pump blood through arteries
They control every voluntary movement

paramedic-r1q4.question: A live electrical cable lies across the only doorway. What comes first?
answers: Step over it carefully
Keep everyone clear and get qualified help to make it safe
Move it with a dry object
Ask a bystander to watch it

paramedic-r6q2.question: A person keeps nodding but has not understood. What should happen next?
answers: Repeat the same explanation more slowly
Ask, ‘Do you understand?’ and continue if they say yes
Shorten the explanation but keep the same terminology
Use plain words and check back

paramedic-r5q6.context: Person A feels well and their observations remain steady. Person B is newly clammy and dizzy, and their pulse has risen across three checks.
paramedic-r5q6.question: Who needs attention first?
answers: Person B, because several changes point to deterioration
Person A, because their observations were recorded first
Both can wait because neither has a named diagnosis
The person with the shorter name

paramedic-r10q4.context: INCIDENT RECORD — An aggressive person is throwing objects near the entrance. Equipment partly blocks the nearest exit route.
paramedic-r10q4.question: What is the safest response to the combined hazards?
answers: Keep clear, move others towards a safer route and alert appropriate help
Approach and argue until the person stops
Retrieve the equipment beside the person before leaving
Ask an untrained bystander to block the thrown objects
